name: hilbert_decode
description: Decodes a Hilbert key back into coordinates. Preferred form: hilbert_decode(key, 'TYPE[n]') with the array type that was encoded (e.g. 'DOUBLE[2]', 'DATE[2]', 'INTEGER[3]'), or a scalar type for one dimension. The original form hilbert_decode(key, num_elements, return_float, return_unsigned) decodes integer and float coordinates; return_unsigned must match the signedness of the encoded values.

name: hilbert_encode
description: Encodes coordinates - one fixed-size array, or two or more separate arguments coerced to a common type - into a single unsigned integer using Hilbert curve mapping. Accepts integer, FLOAT, DOUBLE, BOOLEAN, DATE, TIME, TIMESTAMP, DECIMAL (up to 18 digits) and ENUM coordinates; keys sort like the coordinates in each dimension. Hilbert curves preserve locality better than Morton encoding, making them ideal for spatial indexing.

name: hilbert_decode_bounded
description: Decodes a key produced by hilbert_encode_bounded() with the same bounds and bits, returning the centre of the grid cell as a DOUBLE array.

columns.name: hilbert_decode_bounded(hilbert_encode_bounded(CAST(list_value(12.5, 40.25) AS DOUBLE[2]), list_value(0, 0), list_value(100, 100), 16), CAST(list_value(0, 0) AS DOUBLE[2]), CAST(list_value(100, 100) AS DOUBLE[2]), 16)

name: hilbert_decode_latlon
description: Decodes a key produced by hilbert_encode_latlon() with the same bits (default 32) into the centre of its grid cell as STRUCT(lat DOUBLE, lon DOUBLE).

name: hilbert_decode_latlon
description: Decodes a key produced by hilbert_encode_latlon() with the same bits (default 32) into the centre of its grid cell as STRUCT(lat DOUBLE, lon DOUBLE).

name: hilbert_encode
description: Encodes coordinates - one fixed-size array, or two or more separate arguments coerced to a common type - into a single unsigned integer using Hilbert curve mapping. Accepts integer, FLOAT, DOUBLE, BOOLEAN, DATE, TIME, TIMESTAMP, DECIMAL (up to 18 digits) and ENUM coordinates; keys sort like the coordinates in each dimension. name: hilbert_encode_bounded
description: Scales each coordinate from [min, max] onto a grid of 2^bits cells and encodes the cell with a Hilbert curve. Returns the narrowest unsigned integer that holds dimensions * bits bits. Values outside the bounds are clamped to the edge cells; NaN is an error. Supports up to 64 bits for 1-2 dimensions, 32 for 3-4, 16 for 5-8 and 8 for 9-16. A GEOMETRY value is encoded by the centre of its bounding box (empty geometries give NULL), with 2-D bounds.

name: hilbert_encode_latlon
description: Encodes a latitude/longitude pair with a Hilbert curve over a grid of 2^bits cells per axis (default 32, giving a UBIGINT key). Latitude must be within [-90, 90] and longitude within [-180, 180].

name: hilbert_encode_latlon
description: Encodes a latitude/longitude pair with a Hilbert curve over a grid of 2^bits cells per axis (default 32, giving a UBIGINT key). Latitude must be within [-90, 90] and longitude within [-180, 180].

name: hilbert_ranges
description: Returns the key ranges (lo, hi) of hilbert_encode() that cover the box between min_point and max_point (inclusive, same array type as the encoded values). With enough ranges the cover is exact; when max_ranges (default 64) is reached the ranges become a superset, so keep the exact coordinate predicate in the query. Intended for systems that store or index only the key (key-value stores, other engines, files partitioned by key); within DuckDB, filtering the coordinates of data sorted by the key is usually faster than joining against the ranges.

examples.code: SELECT p.* FROM points p, hilbert_ranges([2, 3]::UTINYINT[2], [10, 12]::UTINYINT[2], 16) r WHERE p.key BETWEEN r.lo AND r.hi AND p.x BETWEEN 2 AND 10 AND p.y BETWEEN 3 AND 12;
